keyVerseText: The elder unto the elect lady and her children, whom I love in the truth; and not I only, but also all they that have known the truth;
rootMeaning: The word Κυρία (Kyría) is the feminine form of κύριος (kýrios), which denotes one who holds supreme authority or mastery, often translated as Lord or master. As the feminine counterpart, Κυρία literally means 'lady,' implying a woman who holds a position of respect and authority. This root connection to mastery and lordship enriches the simple English term 'lady' by suggesting dignity and honor bestowed upon the woman addressed.
usageInScripture: Κυρία appears only twice in Scripture, consistently translated as 'lady.' This limited usage highlights its specificity, referring respectfully to a Christian woman, as exemplified in 2 John 1:1. The uniform translation underscores the term's role as a respectful and affectionate title rather than a generic noun, emphasizing personal relationship and honor within the early Christian community.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding Κυρία as derived from the authoritative title κύριος deepens our appreciation of the respect and honor given to women in the New Testament context, particularly within the church. It reflects the biblical principle that all believers, regardless of gender, are valued members of the body of Christ, worthy of dignity and love. This term also subtly echoes the lordship of Christ, reminding believers that Christian identity involves submission to His authority and mutual respect among His followers. In this way, Κυρία embodies both personal honor and communal faithfulness, integral to the life of the church.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 John 1:1, the elder addresses 'the elect lady and her children,' expressing love grounded in truth. The use of Κυρία here conveys a warm, respectful relationship, highlighting the lady's esteemed position within the Christian community. This word enriches the verse by portraying her not just as a woman but as a beloved, honored figure whose faithfulness is recognized and cherished, encouraging readers to value and uphold such godly relationships.
